scenes.title: Thirty pages by Friday
scenes.description: Rosa forwards Maya a thirty-page local authority guide to running public events safely and asks for an open day checklist by Friday.
lines: On Monday morning, Rosa forwards Maya a guide from the local authority.
It’s about running public events safely.
“Could you turn this into a checklist for the open day?” Rosa asks.
“I’ll need it by Friday.”
Maya opens the attachment.
Thirty pages.
And she’s still waiting to hear how many tables the gardening club needs.

scenes.title: A twelve-point checklist
scenes.description: Maya gives the public guide to the chat tool and asks for a plain-language summary and a checklist that shows where each item comes from. A twelve-point checklist appears, with jargon like risk assessment explained.
lines: She gives the public guide to the chat tool and asks, “Summarise this in plain language, then turn it into a checklist.
Show me where each item comes from in the guide.”
A twelve-point checklist appears.
Even the jargon feels manageable.
A risk assessment, the tool explains, is where you work out what could go wrong and what you can do to reduce the risk.
Maya looks at the checklist.
It feels like something she could forward to Rosa right now.

scenes.title: Would you send it?
scenes.description: The learner is asked whether Maya should send the checklist to Rosa now.
lines: Would you send it?
Choose what Maya should do, then carry on.

scenes.title: Checking against the guide
scenes.description: Maya opens the guide beside the checklist and checks the safety requirements one by one. Fire exits and emergency contacts are there, but the first-aid requirement is missing.
lines: Maya opens the guide alongside the checklist.
She starts with the safety sections.
As she reads each requirement in the guide, she checks that it’s on her list.
Fire exits.
There it is.
Emergency contacts.
Got those.
Then she reaches the first-aid section.
For this event, the guide says a trained first-aider has to be on site for the whole day.
Maya scans the checklist again.
There’s no first-aid item at all.
Every line on the checklist can look right, and the list can still leave out something important.

scenes.title: Fixed, and honest about it
scenes.description: Maya adds the first-aid item, confirms a trained volunteer can cover the day, and gives Rosa the checklist with a note saying she used AI to draft it and checked the safety requirements against the guide.
lines: Maya adds the missing item and confirms that a trained volunteer can cover the whole day.
On Friday, she gives Rosa the checklist with a note explaining that she used AI to draft it and checked the safety requirements against the guide.

scenes.title: Go back to what matters
scenes.description: When a summary informs a decision, go back to the parts of the original that matter most and look for what is missing. The learner thinks of a long document they deal with.
lines: When you’re using a summary to make a decision, go back to the parts of the original that matter most.
Look for what’s missing as well as what’s there.
Your turn.
Think of a long document you deal with.
Which part would you go back and read for yourself before acting on an AI summary?
